title: Autonomix: task-scheduler & telemetry sculptor for runbook microtasks
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Build a modular scheduler and telemetry layer (Autonomix) that compiles runbooks into parameterized microtasks and surfaces safety/rollback signals. Autonomix will accept existing runbook definitions (YAML/typed steps), produce idempotent tasklets that can be queued by event or user-initiated actions, and attach compact telemetry spans to each tasklet for cost/latency/error attribution. Primary goals: 1) enable fast, safe execution of runbook fragments; 2) provide per-step observability for debugging and cost analysis; 3) allow non-engineer responders to launch guarded microtasks from the Console or CLI; 4) support dry-run, canary and automatic rollback policies for high-risk steps.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook-to-tasklet compiler accepts 3 canonical runbook shapes and emits idempotent tasks with typed params
Tasks can be scheduled via API, Console button, and CLI with unified audit trail
Telemetry spans created per tasklet include token_count, duration_ms, worker_id and safety_status
Safety gates allow jobs to be paused on anomaly thresholds (error rate > 5% or median latency > 2s) and trigger rollback policies
End-to-end demo: trigger a parameterized db-migration playlet from Console, run in canary (10%), and abort automatically on regression
Documentation and example runbooks added to Confluence and ops-runbook repo
